reason: H0 exclusively initializes and exercises JSON decoding through wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson; it neither enables an XXHash module nor constructs or updates an XXHash32 hasher. Consequently, it cannot fuzz the changed std/xxhash32 hasher.update! path, especially repeated stateful updates and inputs crossing the 0x100_0000 slicing boundary introduced to keep the length passed to hasher.up! within u32 range. The std/xxhash64 change is comment-only and does not itself expose new behavior requiring coverage.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON, but no XXHash32 module.
H0 calls wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson only; no XXHash hasher API appears.
std/xxhash32 hasher.update! now partitions args.x when args.x.length() > 0x100_0000 before calling this.up!(x: args.x).
hasher.update! conditionally initializes v0, v1, v2, and v3 based on length_modulo_u32 and length_overflows_u32, making update-call sequencing relevant state.
The std/xxhash64 diff only adds explanatory comments and leaves this.up!(x: args.x) unchanged.
recommended_action: Add an XXHash32 fuzz target that initializes a hasher and drives hasher.update! with varied multi-call chunking, including total and individual input lengths around 0x100_0000, then compare digests across equivalent one-shot and differently partitioned update sequences.
